implementation_notes: Ruby has no ring buffer; SizedQueue is the stdlib bounded thread-safe queue (it blocks the producer when full, which is the wrong policy for a lossy audio/stream ring but right for a producer-consumer hand-off). For a fixed, allocation-free numeric ring (audio frames, sensor samples), the array gem's packed buffers or a plain Array preallocated to the capacity with head/tail indices is the construction; Ruby's Array does not need preallocation to be indexed, so the ring is just two integers plus an array you never grow. As in Python, the GVL means a same-thread ring needs no memory barriers and MRI has no atomics, so the acquire/release story does not apply on MRI (it does on JRuby, where two threads can run truly in parallel - so a ring shared between threads on JRuby needs a Mutex or the concurrent-ruby atomics).
idiom_name: SizedQueue (blocking bounded) for handoff; a fixed-capacity Array with head/tail indices for a lossy stream ring
code_sketch:
require 'thread'

# the stdlib bounded queue (blocks the producer when full):
q = SizedQueue.new(256)
q.push(item)
item = q.pop

# a lossy, fixed-capacity ring (drop oldest on overflow) for a stream:
class Ring
  def initialize(size_pow2)
    @buf = Array.new(size_pow2)      # fixed; never grows
    @mask = size_pow2 - 1
    @head = @tail = 0
  end
  def push(v)
    nxt = (@head + 1) & @mask
    return false if nxt == @tail      # full: drop oldest policy -> overwrite
    @buf[@head] = v; @head = nxt; true
  end
  def pop
    return nil if @tail == @head
    v = @buf[@tail]; @tail = (@tail + 1) & @mask; v
  end
end
pitfalls: SizedQueue blocks the producer when full - that is the wrong policy for a lossy audio ring (which must overwrite) and the right one for a hand-off; choose deliberately.
MRI has no atomics and the GVL means a same-thread ring needs no barriers; on JRuby/TruffleRuby (no GVL) a thread-shared ring needs a Mutex or concurrent-ruby's atomics.
The capacity must be a power of two for the mask; a non-power-of-two size needs a modulo.
A ring that grows its backing Array on push is no longer a ring - keep @buf fixed and overwrite instead.
alternative: SizedQueue for a blocking bounded producer-consumer handoff, or a Mutex around a fixed-capacity Array for a lossy ring
